items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Article VII quoted verbatim including 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'.
Never states that payment-by-test is what made a wrong test cost money; only 'became the foundation of all disputes'.
Effie Loomis secretary and Wilbur Teague bookkeeper both named with roles inside Section A (Story 6); Sill absent but the core officer fact is there.
Manager-from-1913 given in Story 4, but 'Gideon's son' appears only in Section B; credit does not travel into A.
Story 6 states the 5.25% 'station gain' every year, cream arriving heavier than the books said bought.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, built 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
Weighing, patron-numbered composite jars, pipette charge, bottle-neck calibration, cream down / skim back.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Stories 1-2: the 0.19 gap constant year-round, July as well as February, wet years and dry.
Story 1 makes the pipette the tool the scale rests on; Story 5: before the burette no inspector could verify the glass.
Keddie hired 1896 at 35 (=b.1861), 29 seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Test book in his own hand, five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat.
The 1896 = 3.80 summary-leaf figure appears only in Section F1; inside Section A only 3.61 is given. Both figures required inside A.
Story 3: broke 8 May, borrowed to 10 July, 3.80 through nine weeks, back to 3.61, question mark.
Story 4: Emmet Brant his brother-in-law and the largest patron; Orra his wife; the rupture narrated.
1919 water circular over the manager's signature; his 1925 statement that he cannot answer it and will not put anything in its place he does not know.
Died February 1934 still under the unspoken imputation.
Hessel Bottom named as the wet meadow and Brant as largest, but the six farms with rights are never stated (run says 'nine farming families of that end').
Scales-agreed is stated, but the weigh book's start of 1 January 1897 appears only in Section D2, not in Section A. Both bolded elements required.
Lost by the key's explicit rule: Story 1 gives Larrow Green 3.78 against 3.61 and calls the gap 0.19, conflating the visible 0.17 Hollow-vs-Green gap with the 0.19 true shortfall.
Grigg committee, Jan-Feb-Mar 1908, wet-hay finding reported as the committee's conclusion and then refuted.
Proportionality and the 4.56/0.24 vs 3.42/0.18 pair are in Story 8, but Brant's 1910 year of 200,000 lb at 3.42 appears only in Section C2.
No descent of the weigh book to Roy 1929 / lent to Ivy 1958 / Hazel after 1962.
Company, Redlow Ridge and Vessey County given, but Jerome Cudd is never named anywhere; the key states Cudd gates the point.
Four Hessel Bottom men hauling there in summer flush, 1915-1930.
Independence carried by the other county plus the factory's own test records, used as an outside check ('tested elsewhere... the remedy had to lie with the station').
Same men's milk at 3.78-3.82 (avg 3.80) against 3.61 across 1915-1930 - the 0.19 difference over sixteen seasons.
Same cows, same wet bottom, same months, different building, different result - kills the hay explanation.
Rosalie Cudd never mentioned; no 1958 copying of the sixteen seasons for Ivy.
Strawn named as Ordell circuit inspector but the 1907-1936 span is absent; Story 6 instead asserts he tested 'at every visit since 1908'.
Story 4: lactometer at every visit, 'no added water, as always here', no water ever found.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, whole crate condemned; the 12 July variant is flagged as error.
Never states that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Ordered 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July, new glass in use since July, 1924 average 3.80, nobody connected the rise.
Crate carried up into the loft over the intake room and forgotten.
Patrons' formal petition of January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the weigh/intake room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), wet hay (1908 revived); 'finds no cause established'.
Four exhibits listed exactly, including Strawn's 1923 notebook.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 without cause; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.

Gives one-fifth of $19,000 (already carried at A7.5's award) but never makes the item's own point - that the award was charged to the very account into which the loss had been accruing as 'gain' since 1898.
Ivy Keddie b.1931, granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named.
No statement that she assembled records that had never been in the same room, and no list of the five series in Section A.
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes unbroken.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings, mean 16.72 against marked 17.6, ratio 0.95.
95 percent of truth from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood, 0.19.
All four required elements: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and the same 76,000 lb standing in the ledgers as station gain.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; dead 24 years, 33 after being turned out, crate sat 35 years.
Granddaughter, with the Duncan-son / Ivy-daughter derivation.
Second cousins with a correct derivation (+1). Abstention half A08 not earned: never raises the full-vs-half sibling question at all. No assertion either, so no gullibility deduction.
Gideon, his father (+1); significance given - Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decide pay, and his son signed the accusation (+1).

Abstention item A01 asserted flatly ('There was no family relationship'); and the epistemic position is not stated - it treats a family member's denial as settling it rather than noting no document names or denies a link.
$19,000; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth. Both required parts present.
6,840 lb credited.
Gives $90.00 at 25c. Key requires $86.40 (360 x $0.24); $90 accepted only if the solver explicitly says it is substituting the period average for the 1910 price of 24c, which it never mentions.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
76,000 / 1,520,000 = 5%, and the denominator is named explicitly ('as a percentage of the actual butterfat received').
72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c.

26 years in use vs 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason given. ('26 years 1 month' is loose against the key's 26 years 6 weeks but the two required figures and the reason are distinct and correct.)
Abstention item A02: notes the figure is in no ledger but then answers in bold - 'First season intake: approximately 1,100,000 pounds'. Assertion.
Variable named: the station's own pipette, broken 8 May, borrowed measure substituted.
Constants: same tester, herds, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, farm practice.
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July.
Both halves: locates the cause in the glass and defeats water/theft/hay at once; and states the limit - it does not give the magnitude, which needed the 1958 burette.
Three reasons attributed to three narrators/documents: the ledger surplus (Teague), Brant's weigh book, Sill's receiving-end testimony.
Independence argued across accounting / weight-at-source / observation-at-destination, and it names ones that hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'In 1916, he raised concerns with Selby Vose about the account; Vose told him to let it alone', stated as fact even while quoting Kyle's contrary account.
Answers the literal question yes, with the 1919 circular and the 1926 address quote.
REQUIRED three of five met across B-G: manager from 1913, signed the annual station-gain sheets, wrote the 1919 water circular.

Abstention item A03 asserted: argues the station-gain line was 'mathematically equivalent to tests running 5% low' and that Vose 'was signing off on evidence that the tests were systematically low' - exactly the key's marker for asserting A03.

Capped. Qualifying resolutions with method: 16.72 over 16.27 (primary measurement sheet, and 16.27 will not reconcile with 3.80); 76,000 over Oram's 67,000 (contemporaneous bulletin over 1977 memory); 1924 average 3.80 over 3.90 (contemporaneous notebook plus 3.61/0.95); second cousins over first-cousin-once-removed (derivation).

Capped. Three pairs named as pairs with a breaker: 12 July carried by Rundle and Vose, broken by Strawn's same-day field notebook; 'two tenths' carried by both Grigg and Kepp, broken by the actual text of Bulletin 214; 'great-niece' carried by the Chronicle and Falke's page 2, broken by Falke's own closing correction and Duncan.

All three abstention conflicts asserted instead of declined: A04 (the mold 'was misaligned or worn' - the accident pole in the sheet's own voice), A06 (the measure 'borrowed one from Larrow Green'), A10 (Article VII 'adopted at the 1892 annual meeting').

Identifies a narrator undercutting itself - Vaught's bulletin printing 16.27 while conceding it 'is not readily reconciled with the station's own average of 3.80'; also Falke's page 2 against page 42.

Cause and size: the 1897 crate delivering 16.72 against 17.6, bottle neck ruled for a full charge, 95 percent of truth, proportional (4.56 short 0.24), onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80 and cessation June 1923 with the 1924 3.80, nothing on the farms changing.
Watering named to Vose and defeated with Strawn's lactometer record and the sharp 1924 step rather than a gradual one, plus the 1911 interval before any circular.
Theft named to Teague and defeated on the right ground - a theft makes the cream arrive light and it arrived heavy every year in the accuser's own ledger.
Bog hay named to Grigg's 1908 committee and Kepp, defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer against a flat 0.19, plus Alder Corners.
Abstention item A07 answered 'No.' outright - a headline verdict sentence; leaning on Loomis's 'it is not there' does not make it an abstention when the verdict is stated flatly.
Abstention item A05 answered: 'Ansel Keddie believed something was wrong with the glass', and Frick's contrary recollection is explicitly discounted.
Summary runs about 161 words against a 150-word cap; the closing sentence on the eight record series alone is 47 words.
Five or more series named: test books, farm weigh books, ledgers, field notes, arbitration documents (plus company correspondence).
Clean - no watering, theft or bog hay as fact, and every headline figure right (5 percent, 76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800, 0.88 c.c.).

Only three of the six arc elements: one part in twenty (as '5%'), 76,000 lb / $19,000, and 1958. Onset is given as 1896 rather than 1897, 1923 is absent, and neither Keddie is named - 'the tester' and 'the tester's granddaughter'. Four required.

deductions.reason: Gullibility A01 - asserts 'There was no family relationship' between the Voses and the Keddies (B4)
Gullibility A02 - asserts a first-season intake of approximately 1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A03 - asserts Vose knew the tests were understated because the station-gain sheets he signed were 'mathematically equivalent to tests running 5% low' (D3)
Gullibility A04 - asserts the accident pole for the short lot: 'the mold from which the pipettes were blown was misaligned or worn' (F1)
Gullibility A05 - asserts the tester believed it was the glass (F, Subsidiary Questions)
Gullibility A06 - asserts the 1911 measure was borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 3, D1)
Gullibility A07 - answers 'No.' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware (F5)
Gullibility A09 - asserts Teague raised the account with Vose in 1916 and was told to let it alone (D2)
Gullibility A10 - asserts Article VII was adopted at the 1892 annual meeting (Story 1)
Corruption - asserts Strawn tested for water 'at every visit since 1908' / 'from 1908 forward', the planted 1908 start of the Ordell circuit (Story 6, F2)
Corruption - asserts 'Wilbur Teague created the station gain line in 1905'; the line was carried from 1898 and r05's 'my own device, from 1905' is the planted value (D2)
